item.title: 5 pitches for The Rock at WWE Survivor Series
item.description: It was announced earlier this week that The Rock will be returning to WWE at Survivor Series next weekend, but the big question still remains surrounding what he’ll actually do at the show in Houston. We don’t know yet if this will just be a one-off, or if it’s going to be a start of a storyline heading into WrestleMania season, especially with the show next spring taking place in Saudi Arabia, who usually pay the big bucks for big stars. We’ve come up with five ideas of what The Rock might do at Survivor Series, and what the fallout from each of them would be. Help The Bloodline in Wargames Feb 1, 2025; Indianapolis, IN, USA; Roman Reigns during the Men’s Royal Rumble match during the WWE Royal Rumble at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images Credit: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The headline match for Survivor Series is The Bloodline vs The 946 in a Wargames match, and it’s sure to be a brutal and chaotic affair. The Rock has very strong ties to The Bloodline, as he’s part of the family that it formed from, and spent a while in 2024 aligned with the faction on TV. So, it’s not out of the realm of possibility that The Final Boss turns out to be the deciding factor in the main event. Cost The Bloodline in Wargames However, just because he aligned with them before, doesn’t mean he will now. There’s still one big match looming that it feels like is still waiting to happen: The Rock vs Roman Reigns. There have been multiple opportunities for it to happen over the years. It was first pencilled in for WrestleMania 39, but that didn’t happen due to The Rock’s movie commitments. Then it was actually announced for WrestleMania 40, but the fan-swell of support behind Cody Rhodes forced WWE to change their plans. WrestleMania 43 is a prime opportunity to do that match, although it would upset some fans, as it has been looking like the planned main event for that show is Roman Reigns vs Oba Femi for a while, and fans are quite heavily behind the rising star. Add to the John Cena Classic Apr 1, 2023; Inglewood, CA, USA; John Cena during Wrestlemania Night 1 at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images The Rock isn’t the only big star who will be at Survivor Series, as John Cena is also set to make an appearance in relation to the upcoming John Cena Classic show in December. Rock and Cena have a stories past together as WrestleMania opponents and with The Rock seemingly inciting Cena’s heel turn in 2025, so it’d be interesting to seem them interact once more. Cut a promo and leave This is the most boring option, but if we’re honest, probably the most likely. Survivor Series will mark the 30 years since The Rock first debuted in WWE as Rocky Maivia in 1996, and just a few years later, he’d be one of the biggest stars in the history of the industry. item.title: Kim Mulkey, LSU headline Thanksgiving week college basketball action
item.description: Thanksgiving week is a special time to celebrate with family and friends, and what better way than to watch some of the nation's best college basketball teams? Three Division I college basketball tournaments will take place in Fort Myers over the next week, with a combined 25 men’s and women’s teams competing at Alico Arena and Suncoast Credit Union Arena. No. 9 LSU (5-0) women’s basketball is one of four Top 25-ranked women’s teams traveling to Fort Myers, along with No. 15 TCU (6-0), No. 16 Washington (4-0) and No. 25 Oklahoma State (4-0). On the men’s side, defending Big Ten Tournament champions Purdue (3-2) will be joining the likes of Pitt (5-0) and Oklahoma (4-1). FGCU men’s and women’s teams are also competing in the field as the representatives from Southwest Florida. Check out the full breakdown of next week’s tournament action: Men's Fort Myers Tip-Off When: Monday, Nov. 23 - Thursday, Nov. 26 Where: Suncoast Credit Union Arena, on campus of Florida SouthWestern The 2026 Sketchers Fort Myers Tip-Off features a 10-team field with representatives from across the Atlantic Coast and the Midwest. The teams are separated between the Beach Division and the Palm Division. The Boilermakers return to Fort Myers for their second appearance in the tournament’s history, having last competed in 2024. Purdue will compete in the Beach Division, taking on DePaul on Nov. 24 at 6 p.m. before playing Oklahoma on Nov. 26 at 12 p.m. Purdue men’s basketball coach Matt Painter is looking forward to seeing how his “young team” can adjust in a new environment, as the Boilermakers have played just one road game thus far in the regular season, losing on opening night against Gonzaga. “ As the game unfolds as we get into the season, you’re not going to shoot the ball well every night, there (are) times when you don’t shoot the basketball well,” Painter said. “Can you still beat a quality team, especially on the road? That’s what you’re really gunning for, you’re gunning to get into these tournaments and to play quality opponents like DePaul, like Oklahoma and have that test. “We’re looking forward to the challenge and we know that both of those teams are going to be tough for us. We have to be ready to take care of the basketball, rebound and defend.” The Panthers will also make their second appearance at the Fort Myers Tip-Off and will be competing in the Beach Division as well. Pitt will face Oklahoma on Nov. 24 at 1:30 p.m. before playing DePaul on Nov. 26 at 7 p.m. Pitt men’s basketball coach Jeff Capel recalled the positive experience he and his team had in 2019 when the Panthers competed in the Fort Myers Tip-Off for the first time. “It was just a great experience for us and when we had the opportunity to join it this year, we were really excited about it,” Capel said. “We’re trying to change habits. item.title: No rest for Michigan basketball as Thanksgiving week brings busy schedule
item.description: The schedule is about to heat up for Michigan basketball. The Wolverines had few days off this week, with a six-day gap on the nonconference slate. But they'll make up for that in a hurry, with Michigan (3-) playing at least four – and potentially five – games in an eight-day stretch to close out November. That begins with a matchup against Villanova (3-2) on Saturday, Nov. 21 (7 p.m., Fox), at Xfinity Mobile Arena, home of the NBA's Philadelphia 76ers . It's a rematch of, among other games, last December's blowout by the Wolverines in Ann Arbor. Much as U-M has, Villanova has turned over its roster in its second season under coach Kevin Willard, with senior Tyler Perkins as the only returning player from last year's meeting. STEP IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION: Michigan basketball finding its identity, forged by foe's speed "It's becoming less and less where there's real continuity in programs year to year," said U-M coach Mike Boynton Jr. With the season still in its opening month, Boynton said he generally likes to focus practices in extended stretches like this past week on self-improvement − working on rotations, installing schemes and identifying solutions to early problems – rather than focusing on scouting reports on opponents. But this week, an illness went through the team in recent days, leaving a number of players were limited or held out as a result. "It's been more individual stuff as opposed to team, which I hate because I would love to have used the time more productively with our whole group," Boynton said. "Just wasn't really an option this time for us." Some of those individual focuses included more reps for Joseph Hartmann, a freshman wing, who returned to the court for the first time in a month Tuesday. Boynton said Thursday's practice would give the team "a little bit better indication" of where his conditioning is, but there's a chance he's available this weekend. U-M also continues to work on Jalen Reed's conditioning. The LSU transfer suffered season-ending leg injuries the past two years and was held out last week against Marquette after he felt a bit of soreness. He's expected to be available this weekend as well. As for the matchup, despite the roster shuffle, the Wildcats have at least one familiar face: Devin Royal – a three-year player at Ohio State and former teammate of Roddy Gayle Jr. – who leads 'Nova at 14.8 points per game and is second at 7.4 rebounds. Cornell transfer Jake Feigen is a sharpshooter, putting up 12.8 points per game on 48.6% shooting on 3-pointers. Perkins also averages 12.4 points per game while Italian freshman center Luigi Suigo, who stands 7 feet 3, is averaging 12 points and 9.3 rebounds. "I think that we're just trying to get better, like each and every each and every game," Michigan guard Kenny Noland said of this week's focus. "I think Villanova is going to be a great test for us. Good program." Villanova is No. 51 in the KenPom rankings, with a top-50 defense (No. 48, 99.8) and offense (No. 50

item.title: Michigan State-Oregon scouting report: Shorthanded Spartans close home slate
item.description: Free Press sports writer Chris Solari looks ahead to the Spartans’ final home game and senior night against No. 14 Oregon : Fast facts Matchup: Michigan State (3-7, 1-6 Big Ten) vs. No. 14 Oregon (7-3, 5-2) Kickoff: 8 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20; Spartan Stadium, East Lansing. TV/radio: Fox, WJR-AM (760). Line: Ducks by 17½. Injury report (As of Wednesday, per BigTen.org) MSU Out: QB Alessio Milivojevic, DT Ben Roberts, S Devin Vaught, LB Jordan Hall, RB Marvis Parrish, TE Jayden Savoury, RB Cam Edwards, FB Jay Coyne, OL Tristan Comer, TE Joe Caudill. Doubtful: CB Tyron Chappell. Questionable: WR Rodney Bullard Jr., CB Tre Bell, QB Cam Fancher, RB Jaziun Patterson, S Michael Richard, LG Conner Moore, TE Brennan Parachek. Oregon Out: QB Dante Moore, RB Jordon Dawvison, DB Aaron Flowers, LB Brayden Platt, LB Teitum Tuioti, DL Matthew Johnson, OL Trent Ferguson, OL Dave Iuli. Doubtful: LB Jerry Mixon. Questionable: DL Bear Alexander. Scouting report When MSU has the ball: With Alessio Milivojevic out for the second time in four games , this time with a left arm injury on top of his right hand issue, the Spartans ’ quarterback situation is again in flux. Cam Fancher is questionable after returning from a right knee injury that cost him four games, only to reaggravate it in Saturday’s 21-14 loss to Washington. That could leave freshman Kayd Coffman to start his second college game after playing a little more than a half in a loss to UCLA on Oct. 24. But MSU also could be without left guard Conner Moore and potentially down its top two tight ends if Brennan Parachek is out (Jayden Savoury has a right foot issue and was on a scooter with it elevated Saturday). The Ducks are tied for 49th in the Football Bowl Subdivision at 343.3 yards allowed per game (133.8 rushing ranks 42nd and 209.5 passing ranks tied for 67th). Oregon allows 20.6 points a game (tied for 33rd), but is coming off a 31-7 smothering of Michigan in which the Ducks held the Wolverines to just 286 yards of total offense and just 71 passing yards. The Ducks have the nation’s 22nd-best third-down defense (32.4%). When Oregon has the ball: The Spartans continue to lose manpower, with Ben Roberts reaggravating an injury after two snaps against the Huskies that kept him out against U-M. They also lost nickelback Michael Richard, who is questionable this week, but did get back cornerback Charles Brantley. Safety Devin Vaught and linebacker Jordan Hall remain out, three key pieces in the middle of the field who will be missing along with Roberts. Still, MSU’s defense is getting improved pressure off the end with the emergence of defensive ends Trey Lisle and Anelu Lafaele and despite the injuries allowed just 192 yards to U-M and 332 to Washington. The Ducks, who lost starting quarterback and Detroit Martin Luther King Jr. High alum Dante Moore to a head injury, continue to move the ball and rank 30th nationally in total offense (426.5) and 26th in scoring (33.8 points). item.title: ‘Can you blame him?’ – NFL fans defend Al Michaels after Texans vs. Colts snoozefest
item.description: Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images Al Michaels has come under a lot of scrutiny this season for his commentary on Amazon Prime’s broadcast of Thursday Night Football. At 82 years old, Michaels is working into the very back end of his career in NFL broadcasting, which has clearly led to some underwhelming performances up in the booth. Fans have expressed their disappointment with some of his play-calling on a number of occasions. Thursday night’s game between the Houston Texans and Indianapolis Colts once again saw a mellow Michaels in the booth. However, on this occasion, NFL fans jumped to his defense following what was one of the most boring games of the season. NFL fans defend Al Michaels after boring Thursday Night Football game The Colts are now seeing out their season after trading away most of their star players. That was on full display on Thursday evening as the Texans only gave up three points in what was never a real contest in Texas. Despite Michaels’ commentary lacking any enthusiasm, NFL fans were largely accepting, given the lack of spark on the field. ‘If you watched the game, this is the interest level he should have had. It was abysmal !! Horrible game to watch,’ responded one fan on X. ‘Do you blame him?? I lost interest in the game as soon as it started,’ added another. The game ended 26-3 to the Texans, with Amazon’s crew taking aim at Michaels during the game with a dig at the amount of vegetables he consumes. The level of interest surrounding the game on Thursday was clearly at an all-time low. ‘The game deserved that level of emotion…’ another NFL fan replied. ‘Just stop. You want him to get excited over that? Are you insane?’ said another. There have been a number of exciting Thursday Night Football games this season, but this week’s was not one of those. ‘In his defense, he was watching this abysmal game at the time,’ replied one NFL fan. While another said: ‘Can you blame him? He’s stuck doing these Thursday night games involving teams playing on just 3 days’ rest. That’s got to be soul-destroying.’ Read more: ‘They hear worse at schools’ – NFL fans have mixed reaction to Texans’ Kamari Lassiter’s viral celebration Tom Brady responds to whether he will come out of retirement and play in the NFL again NFL fans react to ‘generationally bad’ Daniel Jones record after Colts loss

item.title: Drake Allen went from high school manager to Motor City Cruise standout
item.description: For most people, getting cut by your junior varsity basketball team represents the end of their hoops dreams. But for Drake Allen, it was the beginning. The Motor City Cruise guard couldn't imagine life without basketball, so he became the team manager during his sophomore year at Westlake High School in Eagle Mountain, Utah. That meant picking up towels, running the scoreboard, keeping stats, rebounding basketballs during warmups and practice and, if he was lucky, stepping in and playing if they needed an extra guy. "I had a moment that sophomore year where I decided, how much do I love the game? " Allen said. "Am I going to be a manager? And if I was a manager the rest of my life and eventually a coach, that’s what I was gonna be. Just decided to stick around the game as long as I could and it ended up working out." BEST IN THE WEST? How a battered Pistons team solved Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs Thankfully for Allen, he underwent a growth spurt and the rest of his path began to click into place, going from around 5 feet 10 when he was initially cut to 6-4 en route to the Detroit Pistons ' G League affiliate. He played two years at the junior college level before transferring to mid-majors Southern Utah, Utah Valley and then finally two years at Utah State, before joining the Pistons' summer league team this past offseason. Now, he's off to a strong start with the Cruise and proving that there's still more ahead for his basketball journey, which once looked destined for the sideline. "Being able to be a little bit bigger, a little bit more athletic, that all came with time," He said. "But that first year, being able to grow my mind and my love for basketball, it grew even more. When someone takes something away from you, you realize how much it means to you. That’s what happened. Allowed me to become an even better player, I guess." Through five games with the Cruise during the G LEague's Tip-Off Tournament, Allen is averaging a team-high nine assists, along with 16.8 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.4 steals. His 45 assists are the most in franchise history through the first five games of the season, and also leads all G League rookies. Beyond passing the ball, Allen plays both end of the floor. During Las Vegas Summer League, his defensive effort and physicality shined. Allen comes from a sports family – his dad, Roque, played soccer in college, while his mom, Tamra, played volleyball. Allen recalls obsessively watching basketball as a young child, and every day after school. His love for the game only deepened as he grew older. "There’s something you can get better at better every day, and there’s not many things that you can continue to get better at over and over and add new things," he said. "You become obsessed with it, and I think that’s where the love comes from." He wasn't recruited in high school, so he began at Snow College in Ephraim, Utah. He came off of the bench as a freshman but found his footing as a sophomore, earning 35 offers

item.title: How can Ohio State football beat Nebraska in final regular-season road game?
item.description: Here are three keys for No. 14 Ohio State at Nebraska on Nov. 21: Play clean Penalties have plagued Ohio State throughout the season, especially away from Columbus. The Buckeyes have committed multiple false starts in each of their past three road games, including as many as five at Iowa last month. The trend continued at USC , where OSU mixed up cadences, leading to pre-snap issues during freshman quarterback Luke Fahey ’s first start. If they are going to finish above .500 on the road, the Buckeyes must avoid the self-inflicted mistakes that have put them behind the chains. Fahey’s added experience should help reduce communication breakdowns, but the Buckeyes need to be more disciplined across the board in a tough environment. Contain Anthony Colandrea The Buckeyes caught a break last week as Northwestern ’s Aidan Chiles remained sidelined with an injury, sparing them from facing one of the Big Ten’s best dual-threat quarterbacks. They won’t be as fortunate this week with Colandrea behind center for Nebraska. Colandrea leads the conference’s quarterbacks with 447 rushing yards. His legs pose a threat on scrambles as well as designed runs, making it paramount that the Buckeyes contain him in the pocket when plays break down. Colandrea has 22 runs of at least 10 yards, the second-most in the Big Ten behind Indiana running back Turbo Richard. Get off the field on third down Ohio State's struggles getting stops on third down have persisted for weeks, allowing teams to convert more than 40% of the time over the past four games. The defense has proven vulnerable even in third-and-long situations. The Buckeyes ranked 86 th in third-down defense through Week 11. They won’t find much reprieve at Nebraska, as the Cornhuskers can sustain drives. They rank 13 th in the Football Bowl Subdivision with a third-down conversion rate of 47.8%. The Buckeyes fared better against Northwestern, especially late in the game, with more traditional fronts with four down linemen and will look for the momentum to continue. Key matchup Ohio State offensive line vs. Nebraska defensive line It’s no coincidence Fahey put together arguably his best performance against Northwestern. After he was under duress on 32.3% of his dropbacks against Oregon and USC, he faced pressure on just 14.7% of his dropbacks against the Wildcats, according to Pro Football Focus. The protection allowed him to be more efficient and deliver at key junctures of the game. The Cornhuskers present a challenge up front as their 27 sacks are the fourth-most in the Big Ten, and they have posted multiple sacks in all but two games this year, though sack leader Jahsear Whittington will be unavailable. The pass rush puts the spotlight on the Buckeyes’ offensive line and whether they can continue to keep the pocket clean for Fahey after appearing more stable a week earlier. item.title: Top three midfielders in the world? Where Roy Keane-esque Arsenal ace Declan Rice sits in the global pecking order for ex-England star Paul Ince
item.description: Declan Rice Roy Keane - Getty/GOAL Declan Rice has become Roy Keane and Bryan Robson-esque, former England star Paul Ince has told GOAL, with Arsenal’s Premier League title winner considered to be one of the top three midfielders in world football. Ex-Manchester City ace Rodri sits at the top of that talent tree, but an all-action Three Lions talisman has taken up a standing among the global elite. Record-breaking transfer to Arsenal Few could have predicted that would be the case when seeing Rice - who was released by Chelsea as a youngster - step out of the academy ranks at West Ham. No definitive role had been nailed down at that point, with regular game time being seen at centre-half . He eventually settled on a holding role in the middle of the park, with full potential being unlocked in the engine room. Rice captained the Hammers to Conference League glory in 2023. A matter of weeks later, with his stock having been on the rise for some time, a record-breaking £105 million ($138m) transfer to Arsenal was completed - as he became the most expensive British player in history . Game has changed with Gunners Further progression and development has been enjoyed in north London, with the affable 27-year-old now more of a buccaneering No.8 - for club and country - than a water-carrying six that is happy to win the ball and move it quickly on to others. There has been talk of Rice becoming a Ballon d’Or contender , having seen international colleague Harry Kane claim that prize in 2026 , with his value to any given cause clear to see - with a top-flight crown being captured with the Gunners last season. Widely considered to be one of the most complete midfielders in world football, Rice can claim to rub shoulders with the very best in the business - leading to comparisons being drawn with iconic box-to-box performers that once starred for Manchester United and England. One of the best in the business Ince, who filled that role himself for the Red Devils and Three Lions, told GOAL - while speaking in association with freebets.com - when asked if Rice is a top-three midfielder on the planet: “Rodri's the best midfielder in the world. “Jude Bellingham, would we class him as a midfielder? I don't know, he’s probably a 10. I think he's one of the best players in the world, Bellingham, without a doubt. But Rodri is the best midfielder. “Declan Rice, to be honest, has been unbelievable. It was funny because he kind of did the same thing that I did. He left West Ham to go and move on to a bigger club, which I did, obviously under different circumstances. I left West Ham to go to Man United for £1 million and he left to go to Arsenal for £105 million, so there's a slight difference! “I just think he's the all-round midfield player. I really do. I think he's got everything. He can cover the pitch, he can score goals, he's just all-round. You don't really get all-round midfield players nowadays. I think he's probably one of very few who does what he does. He

item.title: UConn women's basketball coach Geno Auriemma sounds off on NIL, recruiting
item.description: STORRS — For decades, UConn women’s basketball could walk into almost any gym in America and expect to be in the conversation for the nation’s best players. Now, as name, image and likeness (NIL) reshapes the sport’s power structure, coach Geno Auriemma says the Huskies are navigating a recruiting landscape where their prestige, winning and player development no longer carry the same weight. “We don't have cachet with guys that are getting a million dollars to go play someplace. They're getting the cachet,” Auriemma said after Thursday’s practice. “I just don't see the value of paying a high school kid a million dollars that hasn't dribbled the ball one time in college.” UConn falls in polls: UConn women’s basketball drops four spots in latest USA Today poll UConn by the numbers: Why UConn women's basketball needs more offense behind Sarah Strong Auriemma’s comments came as UConn’s 2027 recruiting class has taken shape in a way that would have been almost unthinkable for much of his tenure. The Huskies landed five-star guard Sydney Savoury, ESPN’s No. 9-ranked prospect, but missed on several of the nation’s top targets. No. 1 recruit Kaleena Smith narrowed her choices to USC, UCLA and Arizona State after UConn was widely viewed as a contender. No. 2 prospect Ivanna Wilson Manyacka committed to UCLA after the Huskies made her Top 5. No. 8 recruit Haylen Ayers chose Vanderbilt, while Hungarian standout Kinga Josepovits picked Duke. UConn was among the finalists for both prospects. UConn’s success has been built on being the destination for the top players in their respective recruiting classes. Whether that be Maya Moore, Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd or Tina Charles, the Huskies usually have no problem finding the best players in the nation to commit to playing in Storrs. But lately, the effects of NIL have been shown. According to 247Sports, UConn hasn’t reeled in a Top 10 recruiting class in the last two seasons. In 2026, the Huskies ranked 27th, and the year before, they were 17th. Auriemma and his staff have still gotten high-end talent, just not at the same volume. Last cycle, UConn signed five-star center Olivia Vukosa — the No. 2 ranked player in the country. But that was the only domestic recruit Auriemma brought into the program as he filled the rest of his roster with international players such as Jovana Popovic and Marine Dursus. As more schools pour resources into women’s basketball, Auriemma believes the shifting landscape is less an indictment of UConn and more of a reflection of the sport’s growth. “There's more schools that are investing more resources and the players are attracted to places that maybe in the past they weren't,” Auriemma said. “I think the growth of the game reflects that.” As the game changes, Auriemma has not altered his recruiting philosophy. The 72-year-old coach still believes in player development and molding his players through his vision from the time they are freshmen. Paying millions of dollars for a high sch

item.title: UCF basketball travels to No. 16 Vanderbilt: Predictions, TV channel
item.description: ORLANDO — UCF's men's basketball team continues its four-game, non-conference stretch against Power Four squads Nov. 20 with its first road trip of the year. The Knights (4-1) visit Vanderbilt (5-0), ranked No. 15 in The Associated Press' Top 25 and No. 16 in the USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll, for an 8 p.m. tipoff at Memorial Gymnasium in Nashville, Tennessee. Vanderbilt took the front end of the home-and-home series last November with a shooting showcase , knocking down 56% of its attempts in a 105-93 win. UCF proved it could win on the road in SEC territory during the 2025-26 season, toppling Texas A&M 86-74 in College Station. Will the Knights do so again and pocket an early Quad 1 victory towards a potential NCAA Tournament résumé? Here's a look at the matchup, plus predictions and information on how to watch the game on television. UCF men's basketball scouting report Rebounding woes finally caught up to the Knights against Mississippi State. They allowed 17 offensive boards, finished with a minus-20 margin for the night and failed to corral a loose ball after Josh Hubbard's free throw miss in the final 10 seconds of an 86-83 defeat. Dior Johnson continues to carry the offense, leading the nation at 28.8 points per game. Incredibly, the redshirt senior guard is also second only to Ole Miss ' Ilias Kamardine in Division I in assist-to-turnover ratio, dishing out 19 dimes compared to one giveaway. Fifth-year senior Riley Kugel contributed a season-high 12 points against Mississippi State, one of his two prior teams, and Arturo Dean had 18 points on a flawless night at the free throw line (12 for 12). Florida Gulf Coast transfer Isaiah Malone has back-to-back, double-digit scoring performances. — Chris Boyle, Daytona Beach News-Journal Vanderbilt men's basketball scouting report Vanderbilt has gotten off to an excellent start to the season as the Commodores hope to advance further this year after falling one half-court shot short of the Sweet 16 in 2026. Vanderbilt added more size in the offseason to shore up its defense and it's worked, but Tyler Tanner (17.8 ppg) and Ace Glass (17.2 ppg) provide a high-scoring backcourt duo. After them, it's mostly scoring by committee. Chandler Bing is a defensive ace who creates transition scoring opportunities, while Berke Buyuktuncel is a defense-focused big who can pass out of the post. Anthony Brown Jr. is a bench sparkplug who can handle the ball and provides good shooting. Vanderbilt may not be a team that is elite in any one area, but it can do a lot of different things on the court. The Commodores have had some high-scoring wins this season and some where they have won with defense. If one player has an off night, Vanderbilt has plenty of other options it can turn to. — Aria Gerson, The Tennessean UCF vs Vanderbilt basketball game start time, TV channel Date: Friday, Nov. 20 Time: 8 p.m. TV channel: SEC Network+ UCF tips off its men's basketball matchup with Vanderbilt at 8 p.m. from Memorial Gymnas

item.title: Michigan State football picks vs Oregon: Hope for an upset?
item.description: Michigan State closes its home slate for 2026 against No. 14 Oregon on Friday, Nov. 20 (8 p.m., Fox), looking to pull a big-time upset to send Spartan Stadium into the offseason in fashion. Do the Spartans , severely hampered by injuries, have enough to take down the Ducks ? Three Free Press experts make their picks: Chris Solari The Ducks are floating since Jay Johnson took over play-calling, scoring a combined 106 points (35.3 a game) in wins over Northwestern, Ohio State and U-M the past three weeks. The Spartans ’ battered and bruised defense continues its valiant play but can’t slow Dylan Raiola as MSU’s offense struggles to sustain drives. The pick: Oregon 31, MSU 14. Carlos Monarrez The national spotlight comes to Spartan Stadium, on senior night, no less. Unfortunately, Michigan State draws the mighty Ducks, who are ranked 14th and looking to sweep the Great Lakes State in just seven days. Even if you take a savage beating by high-scoring Oregon, hold your heads up high, Spartans, for earning some respect in Ann Arbor. Oh, yeah, and winning the Paul Bunyan Trophy. The pick: Oregon 41, MSU 19 Rainer Sabin After a disappointing 2-2 start in conference play, the Ducks have been on a bit of a heater. They have won three consecutive games, two of which were against ranked opponents. Expect Oregon’s hot streak to continue against a depleted Michigan State squad that will enter this game without a bunch of starters, most notably injured quarterback Alessio Milivojevic. The pick: Oregon 28, MSU 7. Jeff Seidel What a brutal week for Oregon. Having to fly across the country to play a Friday night game. Especially coming off a bruising game against Michigan. Oh. Wait. Oregon crushed Michigan. And the Wolverines are no long so bruising. So, look for Dan Lanning to run it up to try to impress the CFP selection committee. And for Michigan fans to dream: Hey, Dan, you could run down here and stay in Ann Arbor. The pick: Oregon 31, MSU 14. Shawn Windsor Let's give the Spartans a touchdown and a couple field goals, and even the benefit of the doubt when they play their last home game. That they'll be competitive for a moment, struggle to score without their starting quarterback, yet will somehow show the program is heading in the right direction despite all the losing. The pick: Oregon 34, MSU 13. This article originally appeared on Detroit Free Press: Michigan State football picks vs Oregon: Hope for an upset?

item.title: Can UCF football stop Aiden Flora, Iowa State? Scouting report, predictions
item.description: ORLANDO — There's less time than usual for UCF to lick its wounds and turn the page after a disappointing defeat . And the Knights will need every second possible to brace for a suddenly scorching Iowa State offense , powered by the nation's leading rusher. UCF (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) gets a second crack at securing automatic bowl eligibility when the Cyclones (5-5, 3-4) visit the Acrisure Bounce House for the first time. Kickoff is set for 6 p.m. Friday on FS1. Aiden Flora , a former walk-on, earned his third Big 12 Offensive Player of the Week recognition with 216 yards and three touchdowns in Iowa State 's 41-13 blowout win against Cincinnati . For the year, the 6-foot, 195-pound redshirt sophomore has totaled 1,335 yards on the ground with 12 scores. Picked to finish near the bottom of the Big 12 after losing head coach Matt Campbell and two dozen players to Penn State, Iowa State has surpassed 30 points in each of its last three games, prevailing in a 51-49 shootout against Oklahoma State on Halloween. "They're hot right now," UCF head coach Scott Frost said. "They really look like they've found their rhythm the last three weeks, and that's because they commit to what they do — and they've gotten better and better at it. We've got to be ready to handle their schemes, and they do it out of a lot of different formations. I think it's smart what they do. Defense better be ready to come and play physical, and offense is going to have to score some points." UCF dropped its second straight home game on Nov. 14 with a 26-13 defeat to Arizona State . The Knights ran for just 54 yards, their second-lowest output of the season, though Alonza Barnett III went 21-of-30 passing for 257 yards and one touchdown. Can the Knights send their fifth-year seniors out on a high note, or will Iowa State notch its first road win of the fall? The News-Journal's trio of Chris Boyle, Chris Vinel and Ken Willis share their thoughts. UCF vs. Iowa State tale of the tape The Knights put just 16 points on the board in their previous two home games, allowing 10 sacks in those contests. Pro Football Focus grades UCF's offensive line as one of the worst units in the Football Bowl Subdivision — 111th in pass protection (56.7 out of 100) and 114th in run blocking (53.5). It should come as little surprise then that the Knights gain the fewest yards (354.2 per game), convert third downs at the second-worst rate (34.4%) and score the fourth-fewest points (28.4 per game) in the Big 12. "There are things we can do to help," Frost said. "There were a couple plays where ( Arizona State ) got the best of us with the pass rush. I think we did some things later in the game to help that, and we stayed pretty clean the rest of the game. Those guys continue to get better. Everybody needs to be better, to win games in this league, than we were Saturday." item.title: 'Chomping at the Bit': John Carroll returns to the field to face Pahokee
item.description: The waiting is over for the John Carroll Catholic football team . After going 28 days without a game, the Rams finally get to line up against an opponent. They'll return to the field to host Pahokee in a Region 4-1A semifinal. Kickoff is scheduled for 6 p.m. Saturday at McGuire Stadium. It will be John Carroll's first game since a 28-14 loss to Benjamin on Oct. 23. The Rams (7-3) were scheduled to close the regular season at home against Spruce Creek the following week, but that game was canceled because of unplayable field conditions. Following a postseason bye week, the Rams advanced to the regional semifinals when Somerset Prep forfeited its regional quarterfinal matchup. When John Carroll takes its first snap on Saturday, it would be understandable to expect some rust. While the extended layoff may seem concerning, Rams coach Mickey Groody doesn't believe it will be an issue, even against a Blue Devils team that has played three games since his squad last took the field. With his team stewing over its loss to the Buccaneers, Groody thinks the Rams will be ready to go. "It just shows the character of our team. Our guys could've gone in the other direction, but it kind of re-motivated us," Groody said. "Sometimes people say you need a wake-up call, and I think that's what it was for a lot of us. Our guys have been working their tails off since that game, and they are chomping at the bit." Groody said the Rams have embraced the extra practice time, using the weeks between games to clean up mistakes and sharpen their execution. "The past three weeks have been great," Rams junior athlete Kameron Barber said. "Honestly, from my perspective, these have probably been the best practices we've had. We still grinded for a great amount of time. We even had a 6 a.m. practice under the lights before school, and that just shows how dedicated we are to this game and this playoff run. "We've got a chip on our shoulder. We don't want to go out without a fight." Limiting mistakes will be critical for John Carroll as it faces a team it already defeated earlier this season. The Rams earned a 23-20 victory over Pahokee on Sept. 25. The Blue Devils had a chance to tie the game late, but a potential game-tying field goal went wide left. "My favorite moment and favorite game was definitely when we beat Pahokee," Barber said. "It really showed me how great our team truly is. We fight to the end, we stick together and we play all four quarters." Barber was crucial to John Carroll's win that night. The junior recorded an interception that led to the Rams' first score. He later recovered an onside kick and added a touchdown reception. "I do remember my interception in the first half and the onside-kick recovery, but I also remember some crucial mistakes I made in that game. I'm looking forward to this week so I can fix those mistakes." For the Rams to advance, Groody believes his team must improve its pass protection. item.title: Barcelona monitoring 17-year-old Girona defensive talent amid Premier League interest
item.description: Barcelona monitoring 17-year-old Girona defensive talent amid Premier League interest According to ESPN (h/t SPORT ), Barcelona have added Girona youngster Holmes Junior to their list of potential defensive targets as the club continue to assess their options at centre-back. The Catalans are closely following the 17-year-old’s progress, although they face competition from several Premier League clubs who are also monitoring his development. Strengthening the centre of defence has become a priority at Camp Nou, particularly after injuries have disrupted Hansi Flick’s options this season. While experienced options like Alessandro Bastoni are being considered , Barça continue to keep an eye on young talents with a long-term view, leading to their interest in the likes of Ruud Nijstad and now Holmes Junior. Already a first-team player at 17 Holmes Junior has enjoyed a steady rise to prominence since joining Girona’s academy in the summer of 2025. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Girona FC (@gironafc) The 17-year-old starlet spent time in Real Madrid’s youth system before making the move to Gimnastic in 2024 and subsequently signing for Girona, where he has continued to progress. In fact, such has been his development that Junior has already broken into the Girona first-team squad this season, making ten appearances – nine in La Liga 2 and one in Copa del Rey – with even a goal to his name. The youngster has also made four appearances for the Spain Under-18 national team. This potential and rapid ascent at Girona has put him on the radar of clubs looking to invest in promising young defenders, including Barcelona. Barcelona among clubs keeping an eye Along with the immense promise he has shown, what appeals to Barcelona is that Junior is a left-footed centre-back comfortable with playing out from the back, a profile that the club are eager to add to their ranks. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Fundació Futbol Base Reus (@ffutbolbasereus) In addition to that, the 17-year-old starlet is also a versatile player, as he can play in central midfield as well. However, Barcelona are not alone in recognising his potential. Several Premier League clubs are also keeping track of his progress, creating competition for the teenage Spaniard. Junior has a contract with Girona until 2029. While Barça are monitoring him closely, it remains to be seen if they decide to act on their interest or continue to pursue more established names to address their centre-back needs in January.

item.title: Lazio Probable Lineup vs Lecce: Three Defensive Changes & Two Midfield Doubts
item.description: Lazio Probable Lineup vs Lecce: Three Defensive Changes & Two Midfield Doubts For the first time since the start of the season, Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso could make several changes to his lineup as the Serie A leaders resume their campaign by hosting Lecce. The contest will take place at the Stadio Olimpico on Saturday, with the kickoff set at 15:00 local time. Four Lazio Players Ruled Out with Injury While managers seldom change a winning team, injuries and game-time management will force Gattuso’s hand. The 48-year-old lost Josip Sutalo and Nuno Tavares in the draw against Napoli before the international break. The duo joined Mattia Zaccagni in the treatment room, while Adam Marusic may have suffered a new relapse, ruling him out of action as well. Three Changes at the Back Against Lecce According to La Lazio Siamo Noi , Alfonso Pedraza will fill in for Tavares, while Danilho Doekhi regains his starting role due to Sutalo’s injury. The source expects a third change at the back, with Diogo Leite replacing Oliver Provstgaard, who played 180 minutes for Denmark during the international break. Therefore, Romano Floriani Mussolini is the only one who’s expected to keep his place in the backline. Davide Frattesi Hoping to Prove His Fitness In the middle of the park, Kenneth Taylor is guaranteed a starting role, but the other two places are up for grabs. Davide Frattesi left Italy’s camp prematurely due to a muscle strain, but tests ruled out an injury. The 27-year-old immediately rejoined his teammates in group training, so he’s considered the favourite to start ahead of Fisayo Dele-Bashiru. Lazio vs Lecce | Where to Watch, Insights, Lineups & Prediction Rovella & Cataldi Trying to Reclaim Regista Spot Reda Belahyane was involved in Morocco’s double-header against Niger, but he remains the frontrunner to keep his place in front of the defence, even though Nicolo Rovella and Danilo Cataldi have been gaining ground after recovering from injury. Gattuso to Confirm Attacking Trio Finally, the attacking trident should remain intact, despite Albert Gudmundsson’s return to action. Andrea Pinamonti should lead the line, flanked by Tijjani Noslin and Gustav Isaksen. The Dane had a busy international break, but Gattuso cannot afford to drop him, as he’s been a key player in recent weeks, especially in Zaccagni’s absence. Lazio Probable XI (4-3-3): Mandas; Floriani Mussolini, Doekhi, Leite, Pedraza; Frattesi (Dele-Bashiru), Belahyane (Rovella/Cataldi), Taylor; Isaksen, Pinamonti, Noslin.

item.title: Jim Furyk, 17-time PGA Tour winner, will enter Florida Sports Hall of Fame
item.description: Jim Furyk , who won 17 PGA Tour events highlighted by the 2003 U.S. Open , will be among the inductees into the Florida Sports Hall of Fame on May 2, 2027. The induction ceremony will be at the Dr. Phillips Center for the Performing Arts in downtown Orlando, which will be the host for the next three years. Furyk, a First Coast resident since 1995, is the U.S. Ryder Cup captain for the 2027 matches at Club Adare in Ireland and hosts a PGA Tour Champions event, the Constellation Furyk & Friends , which was played for the sixth time at the Ocean Hammock Resort in Palm Coast in October. The tournament has raised more than $5 million for the Jim and Tabitha Furyk Foundation since its first year in 2021. Furyk was ranked among the top 10 in the world for 440 weeks, rising as high as second. He holds the 18-hole PGA Tour scoring record with a 58 at the 2016 Travelers and is the only player to breaking 60 twice in competition. He won the 2010 FedEx Cup and is a nine-time Ryder Cup player. Also going into the Hall of Fame in 2027 will be former Tampa Bay Bucs and Washington Commanders quarterback Doug Williams, who led Washington to a Super Bowl victory in 1988, former NFL players Neal Anderson of Florida and Anquan Boldin of Florida State , two-time LPGA major champion Jane Geddes, baseball manager Don Zimmer and broadcast Paul Kennedy. For additional information and how to purchase tickets for the induction ceremony, visit flasportshof.org . St. Augustine Amateur field finalized Nine players from the USGA Florida Junior Team, Florida Junior champion Easton Oliva and recent Flagler College winner Matthew French highlight the 84-player field for the 21st St. Augustine Amateur Dec. 4-6 at the St. Johns Golf Club in Elkton. Oliva, a Ponte Vedra High graduate, is a freshman at the University of North Florida. French, a Bishop Snyder graduate, won the Jay Jennison Cup in September for his first college title. Among the members of the USGA Team Florida in the field are area players Brady Dougan , Ambrose Kinnare and Jaspreet Kondal of St. Johns County and Jack Cole of Jacksonville. Also playing are Jack Mokris of Winter Park and Junior National players from outside Florida, Fletcher Finch (Alabama), Hill Wang (California) and Carter Graham (Tennessee). The tournament is a World Amateur Golf points event. Nine countries, 18 states and 33 colleges and universities are represented in the field. For tournament information, visit staugustineamateur.com . Middle School Golf program launching The North Florida Junior Golf Tour is inviting First Coast middle schools to join the organizations' Middle School Winter and Summer programs. All area schools are invited to participate. Among the clubs assisting the NFJGTOUR and serving as venues for the classes and matches are the Jacksonville Beach Golf Club, Deercreek Country Club, Blue Sky Golf Club, Blue Cypress Golf Club, Bent Creek Golf Club, The Golf Club at South Hampton and Brentwood Golf Club. item.title: Familiar foe awaits: Vero Beach faces Dr. Phillips in Region 2-6A semis
item.description: The Vero Beach High School football team's march back to Miami goes from one familiar foe to another. Following a first-round victory over area rival Fort Pierce Central, Vero will face an opponent it has seen in the postseason in each of the previous two seasons. Vero Beach is set to take on Dr. Phillips in a Region 2-6A semifinal at 7 p.m. Saturday at the Citrus Bowl. This year's stage is a little different, as the previous two meetings occurred in regional finals. Dr. Phillips captured its third playoff win over Vero Beach in an eight-year span with a 21-14 triumph in 2024. Vero responded with a measure of revenge in 2025, rolling to a 49-23 victory in a game that was even more lopsided than the final score suggested. This season, the Panthers (6-5) have also proven they are comfortable away from home. Four of their six victories have come on the road, including a dramatic 20-19 win last week over No. 4 West Orange in a regional quarterfinal. "They're kind of what you would expect to see in the state playoffs at this point. They've got good players," Vero Beach head coach Lenny Jankowski said. Defensively, Dr. Phillips is led by senior defensive linemen Demarco Henderson III and Yousef Robinson, who have made a habit of wreaking havoc in the backfield. The duo has combined for 31 tackles for loss and 13 sacks. Additionally, sophomore linebacker Kyron Rolle leads the team with 81 total tackles. Offensively, the Panthers are led by junior dual-threat quarterback Tien Williams, who has completed 57% of his passes for 989 yards, seven touchdowns and eight interceptions while adding 469 rushing yards and five scores on 108 carries. Vero Beach knows going in that Williams is the centerpiece of Dr. Phillips' attack. "The quarterback likes to run the quarterback draw. He's going to pull it, and we've got to be ready for that," junior defensive lineman Josiah Taylor said. "We've got to do our job if we're going to dominate and get our offense on the field. We want to do the best of our ability to stop the run game." Jankowski added: "We're always looking to make the quarterback uncomfortable. I think that's especially important this week." During last season's meeting, Williams had -11 yards on six carries. Vero Beach has held opponents to fewer than 100 rushing yards in nine of its 11 games this season. The latest occurrence came during the team's 24-0 shutout of Fort Pierce Central last week. The Cobras managed just 47 rushing yards. Taylor, who tied for the team lead with eight tackles last week, believes the team's work in the front seven is among its biggest strengths. He said fellow linemen Tristan Davis, Alan Carter, Dontallis Render and Kaden Huggins have been instrumental in the team's success. Taylor also credited the defensive coaching staff, particularly position coach Randy Bethel. "They push us every day," Taylor said. "They don't let us slack off. We work hard every day at practice." item.title: Kane trading goals for assists as Bayern await scoring surge
item.description: Kane trading goals for assists as Bayern await scoring surge Despite racking up 43 shots and being denied by the woodwork on three separate occasions, Harry Kane still finds himself outside the top ten leading scorers in the Bundesliga. On the other hand, he leads the assists chart with seven from just nine outings. Quite impressively, this figure puts the Ballon d'Or winner two ahead of his total for the entirety of last season. Goals, however, usually flow from the very beginning. Last season, the net had bulged twelve times by this point – helped largely by a hat-trick that downed Leipzig on the opening day. By Kane’s own high standards and historical record in Germany, his return in the current campaign stands out as an anomaly. Underlying numbers, not least the absolutely relentless shot volume, do suggest that a change in fortune might just be around the corner. In part, you could explain this domestic dip by highlighting his tendency to occupy deeper positions and find the likes of Michael Olise and Luis Díaz on the charge. However, that is very much business as usual in Vincent Kompany’s enthralling system. Champions League statistics do tell a more familiar story, with four in as many matches reminding us of Kane’s potency at the highest level. One moment in particular sums up the England captain’s start: an inch-perfect pass that split Arsenal’s resolute defence in half and put the ball on a plate for Alphonso Davies to finish. As the Allianz Arena awaits the arrival of 1. FC Köln, it simply remains a case of when – not if – this unique goalscoring machine closes the gap to Patrik Schick and a revitalised Niclas Füllkrug.

item.title: FAMU football vs Bethune-Cookman: Who wins Florida Classic? Our pick
item.description: Throw the records out the window; it’s time for one of the biggest rivalries in college football. Saturday is the Florida Classic between Florida A&M and Bethune-Cookman, a Week 12 Southwestern Athletic Conference matchup and season finale for both teams. Kickoff is at 3:30 p.m. at Orlando’s Camping World Stadium. ESPN+ will televise the game, and Tallahassee radio station 96.1 JAMZ will have commentary on local airwaves. FAMU (3-8, 2-5 in SWAC) ended a four-game losing streak at its home finale with a clutch 16-13 win over Mississippi Valley State last Saturday, Nov. 14. The B-CU Wildcats (5-6, 3-4 in SWAC) have dropped three straight after losing to Grambling State 32-21. The school then moved on from fourth-year head coach Raymond Woodie Jr. a day later. The Wildcats named legendary program coach Alvin “Shine” Wyatt the interim for the Florida Classic finale. Wyatt is the winningest coach in B-CU football history. Saturday will be the Florida Classic head coaching debut for first-year FAMU head coach Quinn Fordham Gray Sr. As the Rattlers quarterback, he never lost in the game as a player and briefly held the single-game passing yard record. All-time, FAMU leads the rivalry 54-25-1. However, the Wildcats topped the Rattlers in 2025 with a last-second game-winning passing touchdown on blown coverage. The social media banter between the fanbases has been active all week. But who’s actually going to win this edition of FAMU-Cookman? Let’s meet the teams and predict the score. FAMU vs Bethune-Cookman Tale of the Tape, Florida Classic score prediction The biggest question surrounding FAMU is whether freshman quarterback Armond Parker will play Saturday. He missed the MVSU game, with Gray citing that the young signal caller was “beat up” from the wear and tear of the season . FAMU allows a SWAC-high 33 sacks. James Hayes started instead against Valley and went 14-for-27 for 144 passing yards, tossed a touchdown pass, and had two interceptions. As of Monday’s pregame press conference, the FAMU head coach says he expects Parker “to be okay” to play barring set. The final score prediction will be based on him being under center. If in fact Parker does start, that brings the SWAC’s fifth-best passer back to the Rattler lineup, as he’s amassed1,790 yards through eight appearances and six starts. Parker is sixth with 14 passing touchdowns, but has the SWAC’s second-most picks, 11. Taking care of the football will be paramount: Bethune-Cookman ranks second in pass defense among 12 SWAC teams and leads the league with 13 interceptions. Safety Jaden Davis paces the Wildcats with five. FAMU had its best run game output last week against Mississippi Valley, setting a season-high 166 yards on the ground. Running back Chase Gillespie was the first 100-plus-yard rusher for the team in over a year, with 111. Jamal Hailey added 47. The Rattlers have the worst rushing attack in the SWAC, averaging just 80.8 yards per game, and are also near the bottom of the NCAA Di

item.title: Double injury blow for Arsenal! Mikel Arteta confirms setback as William Saliba & Bukayo Saka updates issued ahead of Newcastle trip
item.description: Arsenal FC v Hull City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal are bracing for a testing trip to St James' Park this weekend as Mikel Arteta manages a squad stretched by significant fitness issues. While one defensive pillar is finally closing in on a much-anticipated return to the fold, the Gunners have been rocked by fresh problems in midfield and attack. Midfield setback tempers Saliba fitness boost Arsenal head into Saturday night's domestic league clash against Newcastle with mixed injury news following the international break. Midfielder Martin Zubimendi has been ruled out for several weeks after sustaining a hamstring problem while representing Spain against England last week, with a subsequent MRI scan confirming the damage. Meanwhile, talismanic forward Bukayo Saka remains unavailable as he continues his rehabilitation from a quad issue that has already sidelined him for five matches. Despite those absences, Arteta received a timely defensive boost on Friday as defender William Saliba is finally poised to join the matchday squad after recovering from a long-term back injury . Saliba has yet to make a competitive appearance this campaign, though he successfully stepped up his conditioning by featuring in two behind-closed-doors friendlies during the recent break. Arteta delivers mixed squad update before Newcastle Speaking to reporters during his pre-match briefing on Friday, Arteta confirmed that Saliba has done enough in training matches to earn a place in his plans for the trip north. "[Saliba] is ready, he’s in a good position. He played two games, he did really well," the Gunners boss said. However, Arteta struck a far more cautious tone when addressing Zubimendi's condition following his early exit on international duty. "[Zubimendi] is out," Arteta added. "Unfortunately he has a small issue in his hamstring. The MRI scan showed an issue there, he’s going to be out for a few weeks." Saka timeline stretches Gunners' attacking depth While Saliba's availability strengthens Arsenal's backline, coping without both Zubimendi and Saka simultaneously presents a stern test of the squad's resilience. Saka is not anticipated to return much before Christmas, leaving Arteta without a key attacking figure during a demanding period. Providing further clarity on the forward's recovery schedule, Arteta explained: "He had another scan. He’s evolving really well, but it looks like it’s going to be an eight-week injury. I think it’s four at the moment so still going to be a while until he’s back with the team." Table-topping Arsenal face tricky Newcastle test Arsenal resume domestic duties sitting top of the table with a five-point cushion over Brighton, making Saturday night's encounter at Newcastle a vital test of their momentum. Protecting that advantage at the summit will require Arteta's stretched squad to adapt quickly away from home.

item.title: 2030: FG takes decisive action to end open defecation with Executive Order
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA – IN a renewed commitment, the Federal Government has unveiled a new Executive Order to accelerate Nigeria’s drive towards ending open defecation by 2030. The unveiling of the Open Defecation Free Nigeria by 2030 and Other Related Matters Order, 2025 coincided with the commemoration of World Toilet Day and the seventh anniversary of the Clean Nigeria campaign in Abuja on Thursday. Vice President Kashim Shettima, represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Delivery and Coordination in the Office of the Vice President, Akubo Adegbe, described the Executive Order as a decisive step towards translating government commitments into measurable sanitation outcomes. Shettima said the order marks a transition from fragmented interventions to stronger coordination, measurable results and sustainable national progress. He called on state and local governments to strengthen accountability, increase sanitation financing and sustain community-led behavioural change He disclosed that since the launch of the Clean Nigeria campaign in 2019, 185 of the country’s 774 local government areas have attained Open Defecation Free (ODF) status, while Jigawa and Katsina remain the only states certified as ODF nationwide. While acknowledging the progress recorded, the Vice President warned that the country still had considerable ground to cover, urging states yet to achieve ODF status to establish monthly and quarterly targets and make their progress publicly available. He also cautioned against a reversal of gains in communities already certified as open defecation-free, stressing the need for sustained monitoring and accountability to protect existing achievements. According to him, Nigeria must prioritise sustainable financing, reliable data, stronger institutions, effective implementation and continuous behavioural change to achieve the 2030 target. He also called on state and local governments to take ownership of the campaign by allocating adequate resources and strengthening sanitation institutions, while urging development partners, the private sector, traditional rulers, community leaders and civil society organisations to sustain their support. Shettima, who chairs the Steering Committee of the Clean Nigeria Project, reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to working with subnational governments, noting that the National Economic Council would also be deployed to advance and sustain the national sanitation agenda. Linking the campaign to this year’s World Toilet Day theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality,” the Vice President highlighted the disproportionate burden poor sanitation places on women and girls. He noted that inadequate access to safe and private sanitation facilities undermines their health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities. item.title: Ubuntu Core Desktop targets 28.04 debut, with default status in its sights
item.description: Canonical is targeting Ubuntu 28.04 LTS for the release of its immutable Core Desktop, with a stretch goal of making it the default download for Ubuntu 30.04. Canonical's VP of engineering, Jon Seager, set out the timetable in his opening keynote at Ubuntu Summit 26.10. Yes, we know, we have heard this before: we reported on his plans last month . But this time, there's the beginning of a release schedule. Seager said that Ubuntu Core is already out there in tens of thousands of IoT devices – which seems like a modest estimate to us, and to him too, as he quickly added "maybe more." Despite some noise a few years ago, though, what's still missing is the desktop version. Seager's slides listed three bullet points: that Core Desktop will be "immutable," "composable," and "attestable." As he put it, they are "taking the whole of the Linux operating system, and cramming the whole thing into snaps." Acknowledging that this is going to be wildly controversial, he said: "This is one for the Redditors." He's right. There is a lot of resistance to snap, and in direct response, advocacy of the Red Hat-backed Flatpak instead – but we have seen almost none that is based on either system's technical merits. Much of that opposition concerns claims of one being more open than the other. We've looked at how both systems work, and our impression is that the implementation of snap is cleaner, simpler, easier to use, and more comprehensible. Snap does depend on systemd, which Flatpak does not – but only for now. Flatpak NG is in development and will also need everyone's favorite init system. Ubuntu Core's immutability is not new technology: even Core 16 is now a decade old. It has supported in-place version upgrades since Core 22. We have reported before that Canonical remains strongly committed to its packaging format, and that commitment seems stronger than ever. Seager continued: "Never has a model like snap confinement been more relevant… we're finally in a position where we can bring this to the desktop." The core idea of an immutable OS is that "much more of the system is not writable at runtime," meaning that it "can't be messed with once the system has booted." He talked about the same three use cases we discussed last month. The "browser-centric machine" is the company's analog to Google ChromeOS, and he said that it's essentially ready now, suggesting that everyone listening probably has a family member whose computer is basically just a way to use a web browser. The second was the dedicated games machine, which we interpret as a response to Valve's SteamOS. This edition, he said, would "boot straight to Steam," with "just enough of a shell to launch games." There's also an immutable "development workstation," and here, he offered the example of developers who need to work on some long-unsupported hardware or software, for whom an immutable OS means that you "can't brick your system by installing some weird old dependencies, unmaintained for 20 years." item.title: ‘There Are People Telling Tinubu Lies About Nigerians’ Support,’ Says Baba-Ahmed
item.description: The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has accused some political loyalists of misleading President Bola Tinubu about the level of public support for his administration. Baba-Ahmed, who once served under the Tinubu administration as Special Adviser on Political Matters in the Office of the Vice President, said the president’s associates could be giving him a false impression of his popularity by relying on assurances from governors and party loyalists rather than listening to ordinary Nigerians. He made the remarks on Friday during an appearance on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief programme. The PRP chairman said his assessment of public sentiment was based on his grassroots political connections and familiarity with the administration, which he initially supported. “I’m a politician. I lead a political party that is entirely grassroots-based. I have very strong organic links with the people. I followed the Tinubu administration from inception. Initially, I was even part of it,” he said. ﻿ Baba-Ahmed said he was familiar with the feelings of Nigerians and was not exaggerating the widespread dissatisfaction with the government. He identified poverty, economic mismanagement, corruption and insecurity as some of the issues contributing to the growing distance between the administration and the people. He also suggested that some political associates were giving Tinubu assurances about his chances of securing re-election in 2027 without adequately reflecting the mood of Nigerians. “There are a lot of people who are telling President Tinubu lies if he thinks himself, and they think that the people are with them. Just look at wherever APC goes. People either chase them away or they trigger violence,” he said. ‘Bamayi’ Baba-Ahmed also described the ‘Bamayi’ chants directed at the president as an expression of widespread dissatisfaction, insisting that the sentiment was not restricted to young people or northern Nigerians. “This Bamayi thing, it’s not just a slogan that young people throw at APC. It’s genuinely an organic element of the way Nigerians, not just northerners, Nigerians feel,” he added. The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja. Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the president’s convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene. The incident attracted reactions from political figures, including Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain Segun Sowunmi, who condemned the protesters’ actions. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the APC campaign council, criticised the destruction of campaign posters and the use of violence during an appearance on Channels Television’s *Politics Today* on Monday. item.title: The BepiColombo spacecraft is finally entering orbit around Mercury
item.description: Artist’s impression of BepiColombo orbiting Mercury ESA/ATG medialab After a long and ponderous journey, the BepiColombo spacecraft will finally enter Mercury’s orbit on 21 November. Over the course of the next year, it will investigate the planet’s geology, its tenuous atmosphere and its magnetic field in an effort to understand how it formed and evolved over time. BepiColombo , a joint mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), launched in October 2018. Mercury’s proximity to the sun makes it incredibly difficult to reach without overshooting the planet and falling into the sun, so the spacecraft had to take a long and looping path over the past eight years, flying past both Venus and Mercury several times and using their gravity to make subtle tweaks to its trajectory. In 2024, an issue with the thrusters lengthened that journey even further, pushing the arrival date back from 2025 to 2026. Now, it has finally arrived. Read more 6 of the most fascinating moments in the life of our solar system While it is arriving at Mercury as a single spacecraft, BepiColombo actually comprises two separate orbiters: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO, or Mio). In December, the two will split apart and move to different orbits – MPO on a near-circular path that takes 2.3 hours to complete an orbit, and Mio on a more distant elliptical orbit, where it will take 9.3 hours to circle Mercury. Advertisement Those split orbits complement the differing scientific objectives of the two spacecraft. MPO is more than twice the size of MMO, and its 11 scientific instruments focus largely on studying Mercury itself . Its instruments include several types of spectrometer to measure the makeup of the surface, a laser altimeter to map its terrain and instruments to study the makeup of Mercury’s extremely thin atmosphere, called an exosphere. Mio’s more distant orbit will allow it to study a broader area around Mercury. It has five sets of scientific instruments to study the magnetic field and atmosphere of the planet, as well as the solar wind that blows strongly in the area close to the sun. Free newsletter Sign up to Launchpad Sign up to newsletter Now that the BepiColombo spacecraft are entering orbit, their primary mission is expected to last only one Earth year, which is a little more than four Mercury years. The mission could potentially be extended for another year, but beyond that the combination of limited fuel and extreme temperatures will make it all but impossible to keep going. Over the course of the year, researchers hope that BepiColombo will provide enough data to solve some of Mercury’s many mysteries. Mercury’s magnetic field is bewildering, because it originates 400 kilometres above the planet’s centre and should have faded away long ago. Its atmosphere must be continuously supplied with material from the surface, but we are unsure exactly how that occurs.

item.title: Support tech fixed malware by charging client less for their services
item.description: Welcome to Friday and therefore to another edition of On Call , The Register 's reader-contributed tech support column in which we share your tales of cleaning up messes made by clients and colleagues. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Dennis" who told us he once ran a tech support business in a major US city. "I got a call from a very well-known lawyer's office," he told On Call. "Over the two decades I spent supporting his office, this attorney and I became close friends." The attorney was also a good client because Dennis found himself billing a three-figure sum every month for malware removal that resulted from the lawyer’s – ahem – personal browsing habits. Dennis eventually tired of malware removal and told his client to expect a substantial bill for the iMac he was about to buy as a replacement for his PC. "I told him this would pay for itself in 18 months," Dennis wrote, because he figured it wouldn't get malware all the time. "He actually said, with genuine concern: 'If you do that, you will make less money'." Dennis replied that he aimed to give his clients the best advice, and that on this occasion his counsel was to pay Apple instead of himself! "It took him about five years to stumble across anything that could harm that iMac," Dennis wrote. "When he did, I had no idea what to do: I had never seen an infected Apple product." So he did what all tech support people do: reinstalled the OS and crossed his fingers. Dennis was rewarded when the machine came back to life, with all data and settings intact. "I had given up at least $6,000 in support revenue by solving his problem and I'd do it again," he wrote, before winding up his story by letting us know "I retired five years ago. It’s still on his desk!" Have you done less tech support to deliver more value? If so, click here to send On Call an email and charge us with the responsibility of telling your story on a future Friday. ®

item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 20, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira continued to face downward pressure against the United States dollar across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market on Friday, November 20, 2026, driven by tightening foreign exchange supply and rising end-of-year seasonal demand. Official Market Performance Real-time interbank spot tracking at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market placed the US dollar at ₦1,352.54 during early morning trading on Friday, following an opening rate of ₦1,351.86 and an intraday peak of ₦1,355.31. This early session trading follows Thursday’s official Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) volume-weighted benchmark, which saw the naira depreciate to a four-month low. According to official CBN data for the November 19 trading session, the NFEM weighted average rate settled at ₦1,376.58 per dollar, while the indicative closing rate rose to ₦1,388.00 per dollar from ₦1,379.99 recorded on Wednesday. Intraday interbank transactions on Thursday were conducted between a low of ₦1,370.00 and a high of ₦1,397.00 per dollar. Despite the depreciation, market liquidity improved significantly, with NFEM interbank turnover surging by 59.13 percent to $800.31 million across 184 deals, up from $502.88 million the previous day. Parallel Market Rates In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the local currency weakened further as Bureau de Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a selling rate of up to ₦1,468 per dollar on Friday morning, following Thursday’s close between ₦1,461 and ₦1,468. Buying rates among informal currency dealers hovered between ₦1,445 and ₦1,458 depending on transaction volume and location. With Thursday’s official closing benchmark at ₦1,388.00 and parallel market quotations reaching ₦1,468.00, the spread between the official and unofficial windows widened to ₦80.00 per dollar, compared to ₦70.01 recorded earlier in the week. Market Drivers and Reserve Outlook Since the end of October, when the naira closed at ₦1,346.00 in the official window and ₦1,373.00 in the parallel market, the currency has lost ₦42.00 and ₦95.00 in the respective segments. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.71 billion as of November 18, 2026, reflecting a moderation of $554 million from the October 27 peak of $55.26 billion. Financial analysts note that the recent divergence between both windows is largely fueled by heightened festive import demand, corporate obligations, and reduced autonomous foreign exchange inflows rather than a structural depletion of the country’s external reserves. item.title: Why we pulled down Umeh’s billboard — Anambra govt
item.description: The Anambra State Government has dismissed claims that a billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh was pulled down because it carried the image of former Governor Peter Obi, calling the allegation false and misleading. The government said the enforcement action stemmed from an alleged violation of the Anambra State Signage Act, 2010, rather than the identity or political affiliation of anyone featured on the billboard. In a statement issued yesterday, the Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, said that although Senator Umeh had paid the required signage fee, Peter Obi had not complied with the payment requirement. Mefor alleged that the senator, instead of fully complying with the law, used the billboard to promote the presidential candidate of the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), thereby contravening the state’s signage regulations. He stressed that the removal was carried out strictly in accordance with the law, which he noted was enacted during Peter Obi’s administration as governor of Anambra State. “For the avoidance of doubt, the billboard was not pulled down because of Peter Obi’s image,” the commissioner stated. The government further warned that any combined billboard campaign featuring candidates who had not fulfilled their signage obligations would face similar enforcement, regardless of their political party, status, or affiliation. It maintained that the state’s outdoor advertising regulations would be guided by fairness, transparency, and even-handed application of the law. Mefor urged the public to disregard what he described as a misleading narrative surrounding the incident, insisting that the government remained committed to due process and equal treatment in enforcing existing laws. Vanguard News The post Why we pulled down Umeh’s billboard — Anambra govt appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 53 Years Later, The Greatest Closing Line In Sci-Fi History Is Still The Best Book Quote Of The 1970s
item.description: The canon of science-fiction literature is home to countless unforgettable endings, from 1984 ’s short but devastating retrospective ("He loved Big Brother") to The Three-Body Problem ’s defiant reminder that humanity cannot be so easily wiped out. The best sci-fi endings don't offer comfortable closure. Instead, they reframe everything that came before. In their closing lines, great sci-fi novelists leave readers suspended in the aftermath, forced to stew in the terrifying logic of cold technology, the fragility of human nature, and the vast expanse of space.
